cards.name: Ken Burns pan and zoom on a still
cards.summary: A documentary still drifts: a slow 15% push-in while the frame tilts down the photo, built from the clip zoom ramp plus Transform position keyframes so both apps get the same move.
use_for: a still that must hold 4-8 s under narration
portrait (4:5 or 9:16) photos in a 16:9 edit, using their spare height for the tilt
avoid: pushing past about 20% on a low-resolution scan (softness shows)
a horizontal pan at zoom 1.0 on a photo that only just covers the frame width: it exposes the edge
faces cut by the frame edge at the end of the move
cards.keyframes_note: Spec: example/still.png (1080x1350) cover-fits a 1920x1080 frame at 177.8%, leaving 660 px of spare height above and below and none at the sides, so the pan is vertical only. 'zoom' 1.15 is the bridge's own scale ramp over the clip (100% -> 115% of the cover-fit scale, linear, both apps). The pan is the Transform effect's Position: After Effects in layer pixels of the 1080x1350 still (centre [540, 675]; 600 -> 750 = 150 layer px = about 267 frame px); Premiere as fractions of the CLIP's own frame (x = fraction * source width, y = fraction * source height, not of the sequence frame): 0.4444 -> 0.5556 = the same 600 -> 750. Measured 2026-10-13 on a 1080x1350 dot probe in a 1920x1080 sequence: [0.5, 0.4444] put the source centre at source px (539.7, 600.0) in Premiere and (539.7, 599.9) in After Effects at 0 s, and (539.8, 748.8) in both at 5.95 s (spec 748.75). The sequence-frame reading would have meant (960, 480). The bridge keys are linear; for an eased move sample the curve (see 'Eased slow push-in'). Premiere also accepts a clip 'pan' ([[x, y] start, [x, y] end], Motion Position in sequence fractions) and 'zoom_from', but ae_build.jsx ignores both, so this recipe keeps to keys both apps build. Working defaults: 10-20% over 5-8 s.
built_from: Keyframe interpolation, easing and the Graph Editor
Ken Burns move (stills pan and zoom)

verified.note: On the dot probe the move lands exactly on the spec: source px (539.7, 600.0) at 0 s and (539.8, 748.8) at 5.95 s, scale 178% -> 204-205%, so Premiere read Position as fractions of the clip's own frame; the recipe's own gradient still drifts the same way (Premiere vs After Effects mean |luma| 0.03-0.04).

ae.note: After Effects put the probe dots at source px (539.7, 599.9) at 0 s and (539.8, 748.8) at 5.95 s with scale 178% -> 204%, the same move as Premiere (mean |luma| difference 0.01).

cards.name: Eased slow push-in
cards.summary: A gentle 10% push over 6 s that starts and lands softly: the ease is built from five Transform scale keys sampled on a smoothstep curve, because the bridge writes linear keyframes.
use_for: interview or presenter shots that need life without a visible zoom
a hold on a key line of VO
the last shot before a cut to black
avoid: fast cutting (a 2 s shot gets 1-2% of visible motion)
pairing it with the clip 'zoom' ramp (double zoom)
cards.keyframes_note: Keys at 0, 1.5, 3, 4.5 and 6 s hold 100, 101.56, 105, 108.44 and 110% (3u^2 - 2u^3, the curve AE Easy Ease and Premiere's dissolves follow per the bridge README); linear interpolation between five samples is close to a true ease at this speed. Both apps scale around the layer centre (the Transform anchor default). With Uniform Scale on, Scale Height is the one that counts; Scale Width is set to the same keys so the move survives either reading. Times are from the clip start; for another length scale the key times.
built_from: Keyframe interpolation, easing and the Graph Editor

verified.note: A slow, steady push-in over the clip, frame by frame the same as After Effects.

ae.note: The same push as Premiere (mean |luma| difference 2.6).

cards.name: Focus pull in (blur to sharp)
cards.summary: The shot opens out of focus and sharpens in 0.8 s, a 2D stand-in for a lens focus pull on the first beat of a scene.
use_for: a reel's first frame that should read as 'arriving'
avoid: a real rack focus between two subjects (needs separated planes or a 3D camera: see the camera DOF card)
long holds of blurred picture under important lower thirds
cards.keyframes_note: Same engine in both apps: After Effects 'Gaussian Blur' (ADBE Gaussian Blur 2) is Premiere 26's 'Gaussian Blur (Legacy)', with the same Blurriness and Repeat Edge Pixels (PVE Gaussian Blur card), so the two builds should match. Blurriness 30 -> 0 over 0.8 s (linear keys). The blur acts in layer pixels before the layer's cover-fit scale, so on a source smaller than the frame it looks stronger. 'zoom' 1.04 adds a small settle. A true rack focus: 'Camera depth of field and rack focus' tool card.
built_from: Camera depth of field and rack focus

verified.note: Soft at 0.6 s and sharp from 2.4 s on, the blur-to-sharp opening the summary describes.

ae.note: The same blur and sharpening as Premiere (mean |luma| difference 2.6-2.8).

cards.name: 2.5D photo parallax (two planes)
cards.summary: A photo split into a clean background plate and a cut-out subject: the subject drifts and grows faster than the background, which reads as depth. Built as an After Effects VFX scene, no 3D camera needed.
use_for: archive or press photos in documentaries
turning a still hero image into a 6 s shot
avoid: photos where the subject cannot be cut out cleanly (hair against a busy background)
moves so large that the clean plate's filled-in area becomes visible
cards.keyframes_note: Scenes for vfx.render_scenes(scenes, aep, out_dir) at 1920x1080 25 fps. Inputs to prepare: parallax/bg_clean_plate.png (the photo with the subject removed: Content-Aware Fill or Photoshop Generative Fill) and parallax/subject_cutout.png (the subject on transparency, straight alpha), both 1920x1080 so the footage layer's cover-fit scale is 100% and the scale segs can be absolute (112% = zoom 1.12). The background moves 40 px and scales 112 -> 114%; the subject moves 120 px and scales 112 -> 119%: the subject:background speed ratio (3:1 here) sets the perceived depth. Segs are linear for a constant drift. True 3D (cards at different Z under a camera) is in 'Photo parallax with 3D layers and a camera'.
built_from: Footage interpretation (FootageSource: frame rate, loop, alpha)
Photo parallax with 3D layers and a camera

verified.note: The cut-out subject drifts and grows faster than the clean plate behind it, which reads as depth; the subtle 24 px feathered edge shows as a soft halo.
